stories.headline: Abdusattorov beats Caruana in a double-rook ending
stories.body: Nodirbek Abdusattorov beat Fabiano Caruana with White in round 9 of the Olympiad in Samarkand, in Uzbekistan's match with the United States. It turned on the last move before the time control: 40...Rxb3, played with 40 seconds left on the clock, took the engine's assessment from a small edge for White to a winning one. The engine preferred 40...Rh3+. The breakthrough came with 44.Rxg7+, and Abdusattorov won in 49 moves.

stories.headline: So beats Sindarov as the United States meet Uzbekistan
stories.body: Wesley So beat Javokhir Sindarov with White in round 9, on another board of the same match as Abdusattorov–Caruana. The engine marks 41...Re2 as the moment White's clear advantage became a winning one; it preferred 41...Rc4. White doubled rooks on the seventh rank, and So won in 48 moves.

stories.headline: Praggnanandhaa and Keymer draw after 57 moves
stories.body: R Praggnanandhaa and Vincent Keymer drew in round 9, India against Germany. It was a Closed Ruy Lopez that went the distance: the queens came off on move 54, and the bishop ending that was left was drawn three moves later.

stories.headline: Vachier-Lagrave and Ding draw in a rook ending
stories.body: Maxime Vachier-Lagrave and Ding Liren drew in round 9, France against China. A Closed Ruy Lopez ended on move 43 in a rook ending with three pawns each, all of them on the kingside.

stories.headline: Vakhidov beats Giri, rated 230 points higher
stories.body: Jakhongir Vakhidov, of Uzbekistan's second team, beat Anish Giri with White in round 9 against the Netherlands. Giri is rated 2757 and Vakhidov 2527. The engine marks 43...d3 as the move that decided it, taking White's clear advantage to a winning one; it preferred 43...Ke6. White went on to queen a pawn on c8, and Vakhidov won in 53 moves.

stories.headline: Rapport beats Alekseenko in 38 moves
stories.body: Richard Rapport beat Kirill Alekseenko with White in round 9, Hungary against Austria. 24...g4, played with nine minutes left on the clock, is where the engine's assessment went from a clear advantage for White to a winning one; it preferred 24...Rad8. Rapport won in 38 moves.

stories.headline: Zhu Jiner beats Mkrtchian in the Women's Olympiad
stories.body: Zhu Jiner beat Lilit Mkrtchian with White in round 9 of the Women's Olympiad, China against Armenia. From 45...Bc1 the engine rated White's position as winning and went on rating it so; it preferred 45...Bg5. Zhu Jiner won in 55 moves.

stories.headline: Assaubayeva wins with Black against Mungunzul
stories.body: Bibisara Assaubayeva beat Bat-Erdene Mungunzul with Black in round 9 of the Women's Olympiad, Kazakhstan against Mongolia. The game turned on 50.Be2, played with under six minutes left: the engine's assessment went from a clear advantage for Black to a winning one, and 50...Be4+ followed at once. The engine preferred 50.Rf2. Assaubayeva won in 51 moves.
